transcript.text: My Miele dryer takes ages now and keeps flashing a filter warning even though I clean the fluff filter in the door every time. Is it on its way out?

The type of tumble dryer you have changes what we need to check next, as each model handles moisture differently. This helps us understand why your clothes are taking much longer to dry and remain damp. To guide the right checks, could you tell me if it is a vented dryer (with a hose out of the back), a condenser dryer with a water container, or a heat-pump dryer?
It's a heat pump dryer - a Miele T1. No burning smell or anything like that, it just takes much longer than it used to.

Thanks for confirming your Miele T1 heat-pump dryer is taking much longer to dry clothes that remain damp. To help us pinpoint why it isn't heating effectively, we need to check the temperature during operation. Partway through a drying programme, is the air and the laundry warm, or completely cold?
It does get warm - the drum turns, the clothes are warm and the water container fills. It just takes over 3 hours now, and the filter light comes on mid-cycle with some loads.

Thanks for letting us know about the drying issues. Overloading the machine or putting in clothes that weren’t spun properly in the washer can make drying much slower. Please ensure the drum is no more than about two-thirds full to help with efficiency. Was it overloaded or were the clothes very wet going in (and have you changed that), or was it a normal, well-spun load?
It's mostly towels and bedding, usually a normal load that's been spun in the washer as usual. I don't think I've overloaded it, and nothing has changed on that front.

Thanks for confirming that. Please switch the dryer off, unplug it and let it cool down first. Behind the flap at the bottom front there's a condenser unit (or a second filter on heat-pump models). Take it out and rinse the fluff off under the tap, then let it drip-dry and refit it. You can see where this is in the picture below. Was it clogged with fluff (and is it clean now), or was it already clean?
[Helpful to see: image "Where the condenser and water tank are" — On a condenser dryer the water container pulls out at the top and the condenser/heat exchanger sits behind a flap at the bottom front — slide it out and rinse it. Condenser/heat-pump dryers only; layout may differ.]

I didn't know there was a second filter. I found it behind the bottom flap and it was completely matted with fluff. I've cleaned it. There's also a felt-like layer of fluff on the fins behind it, should I do anything about that?

Thanks for letting us know you’ve cleaned the condenser. Please run a normal drying programme using a normal load of laundry. This will help us see if the issue is resolved after the maintenance step. Is the laundry coming out dry now, or still damp?
I vacuumed the fluff off the fins gently with a brush, then ran a normal load. It dried in just over 2 hours and there was no filter warning this time.

[Heading: Clogged condenser]
That’s great news to hear your Miele T1 dryer is working normally again. It appears a clogged condenser was the likely cause of the issues you experienced, such as longer drying times and the container filling up quickly. Since this has been resolved by cleaning the condenser, no replacement parts are needed. We’re glad it’s back to its usual performance with your normal load.
